rules: Every fact is from the capture, as the researcher wrote it: names, roles, organisations and countries as Web Summit's speakers page shows them, in its first view on 8 November. The curator added none, checked none and rewrote no source. Public, professional information only; nobody here who the page does not list as a Web Summit speaker.

captures.what_is_new: Twenty speakers from the first view of the speakers page, with role, organisation and country, grouped by the researcher into five themes: robotics and embodied AI; AI models and products; mobility and devices; internet infrastructure and security; investment, policy and economics. Two of the twenty are robots.

duplicates_and_noise.item: The robotics and embodied AI group (Li Chen, William Shi, Yuli Zhao, the two robots)
duplicates_and_noise.why: The published article 'Following robotics at Web Summit' and its draft already name Unitree's and AgiBot Europe's speakers and the robot speakers (S12, S15).

duplicates_and_noise.item: The investment, policy and economics group; the mobility and devices group; the infrastructure and security group
duplicates_and_noise.why: Each is thin without what the organisations do, which the capture says is not captured yet; the researcher's next pass adds it. Revisit at the next run.

for_the_fact_checker.what: Only the page's first view was read and its order rotates, so the five are a sample of the lineup, not the lineup; the story must say so. Countries are as the page shows them. What each company does is not in the capture.

story_candidates.title: Five AI builders on Web Summit's speaker list worth knowing
story_candidates.angle: A theme-led guide for founders building with AI: Tao Zhang (Manus AI), Dahai Li (ModelBest), Alan Shen (MiniMax), Richard Socher (You.com) and Michele Catasta (Replit), who they are by role, what their companies build, and why a founder in the field might want to hear them, from the speakers page as read on 8 November.
story_candidates.note: Theme-led (standing answers 19, 20): different from S12 and S15, which cover the robots and the robotics speakers, and from S16, which covers European help for AI startups; no article or draft names these five. What each company does is not in the capture: journalist-connections takes it from each company's own public page and re-reads the speakers page the same day. Wording: never say these people will meet anyone or are interested in anyone.
